subject: Re: Request for penetration test evidence following regional incident
messages:
From: Stephanie Lang <stephanie.lang@rivertoncapital.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Holt <chris.holt@rivertoncapital.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Penetration test evidence request — post-regional incident

Sergio,

Thanks for the quick responses in the status call earlier. After our SOC & ops team reviewed the incident bulletin published this morning, Riverton leadership asked for the most recent penetration test evidence you can share that relates to the public-facing inference endpoints. Specifically:

- A redacted executive summary of the latest pen test (high/med/low findings and fixes applied)
- Scope: confirmation of whether the test included the multi-tenant hosted API and token-handling flows
- Remediation status and dates for fixed items (or a tracker)

We understand full reports may be confidential. A redacted summary plus a list of open/closed items with dates would suffice for our audit. Can you confirm whether Redwood can share that and an ETA? Our compliance deadline to close the loop internally is May 7.

Appreciate it —
Stephanie
Senior VP, Security & Compliance
Riverton Capital

Attachments: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Lang <stephanie.lang@rivertoncapital.com>
Cc: Chris Holt <chris.holt@rivertoncapital.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:01:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Penetration test evidence request — post-regional incident

Stephanie —

Thanks for the note and for outlining the asks. Short answer: yes, we can provide a redacted penetration test summary and a remediation tracker that covers the scope you listed. A few quick clarifications so we deliver the right artifacts:

- Which environments are you most concerned about? (hosted API / dedicated pools / Private VPC)
- Do you need CVE-level patch timestamps or just remediation completion dates?
- Is Riverton's audit team able to sign an NDA that covers the full report if needed?

I want to loop in our security lead and compliance PM to produce a summary that matches your audit needs. I can get a redacted summary and a CSV-style tracker by EOD today for the items we can share; full report access will need the usual controls.

I'll add Marissa (security) and Laura (compliance) to coordinate delivery and redaction.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Stephanie —

Marissa from Security here. Sorry to jump in mid-thread. Quick context: Redwood completed a third-party penetration test in February 2026 that covered our hosted inference control plane and public API endpoints; dedicated and private installations were included on a sample-basis (configured tenant instances). The test vendor was RedCrest Labs; findings were triaged by our engineering teams and tracked in our remediation tracker.

What we can provide immediately (redacted where appropriate):
- Redacted executive summary (high-level findings, impact assessment, and remediation status)
- CSV tracker with open/closed items, severity, owner, and remediation completion date (or planned date where still open)
- A one-page note describing scope & testing methodology (types of tests performed, sample environments inspected)

What we cannot share publicly: raw exploit steps and full vulnerability PoCs. For customers with strong need, we can provide the full report under a bilateral NDA and controlled access.

I'll attach the redacted summary and the tracker in a minute. If you need CVE patch timestamps, say so and we'll extract them from the tracker.

Marissa Cole
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: riverton_pt_summary_redacted-2026-04-30.pdf (PDF, redacted), remediation_tracker-rc-2026-04-30.csv (CSV)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Lang <stephanie.lang@rivertoncapital.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 14:20:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: Penetration test evidence request — post-regional incident

Hi Stephanie —

Following up on Marissa's note. Attached are the redacted executive summary and remediation tracker we discussed. Summary notes:

- Scope: primary focus on hosted inference API (token handling, model input validation, rate-limiting enforcement); sample tenant instances for Dedicated were included. Private/VPC installs are out of scope for this report unless a customer requests a directed assessment.
- Findings: 3 high (one token handling race condition, two auth misconfigurations in third-party integrations), 7 medium, 12 low. All high items show remediation completed by 2026-03-18 with post-fix validation.
- Open items: 2 medium items planned (ETA 2026-05-14) — listed in tracker with owners.

If Riverton requires the original RedCrest report or CVE timestamps for your internal artifact, we can arrange NDA and a secure transfer. If you prefer, we can also set a short call with Marissa + engineering owner to walk through the high items and the post-incident mitigations.

Laura Bennett
Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: riverton_pt_summary_redacted-2026-04-30.pdf, remediation_tracker-rc-2026-04-30.csv

Laura / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple of quick follow-ups from our SOC review:

1) For the token-handling race condition you listed as remediated on 2026-03-18, can you provide the engineering commit id or CVE (if assigned) and the time the patch was deployed to production?
2) For the two medium items still planned, please confirm whether any compensating controls are in place in the interim; we need that for our risk acceptance form.

If it's easier, we can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow morning. Otherwise, if you can send the commit IDs and short notes on compensating controls, we'll proceed with internal sign-off.

Appreciate the help —
Chris
Director, Platform Security
Riverton Capital
